_README: THE SCENARIO LIST IS DATA, NOT CODE — design Q182: 'we are still on first review pass we could
add more'. Adding a preset is editing this file: no GDScript change, and the inspector dropdown
in Tools/spotlight_tool.tscn is built from this list at load time.
THE BOARD IS THE REAL PLAY-AREA GEOMETRY. A column stacks: each card past the first shows only
its top STRIP (CardVisual.card_separation_play_custom) while its art hangs a full card below —
PlayArea.slot_center_global's own pitch. 'depth' is how many cards deep every column is, so a
depth of 3 means two covered cards under each visible one.
Fields:
cols, depth      the board. depth is the STACK height, and stacking is what buries a card.
lit              [[col, depth], ...] — one section. Slots are 0-based.
sections         [ [[col,depth],...], ... ] — A CASCADE. Each entry is one scored section, and
the tool walks them in order, pulsing the show once per section (GAP-006) and
REPLACING the light set without freeing it (which is what chart E's travel
needs: 'no instant movements or spawning in and out'). Use this or 'lit'.
casual           true = a MOCKED SOLO ACTIVATION TRIGGER, not scoring. Chart T's momentary cue,
which fires whenever a card becomes active in ordinary play, at Q245=(c)'s
shallower dim.
row_separation   true = open the lit row from a strip to a full card (the S16 reveal,
SIMULATED — PlayArea cannot do this yet).
proves           what you are meant to be looking at.
Inspector toggles cut across every preset: 'play' walks the cascade, 'section' holds one,
'revealed' holds the show up for a still, and 'row_separation'/'separation_amount' open the row.

scenarios.name: Flat board, one row lit
scenarios.proves: The no-expansion path — the baseline every other preset is read against

scenarios.name: STACKED — a buried row lit, separation OFF
scenarios.proves: Why S16 is needed. Every column is 3 deep, so the lit cards show only their strip and their art square is hidden underneath. This is what a circle lands on today.

scenarios.name: STACKED — the same row, separation ON
scenarios.proves: The S16 reveal, simulated: the lit row opens to a full card and the rows below move down. Compare directly against S2 — this is the before/after the reveal exists to produce.

scenarios.name: A full row of 5
scenarios.proves: Origin spread across the whole board width — change screen_size and watch the beams re-fan

scenarios.name: A COLUMN section, stacked
scenarios.proves: Beams converging down one x onto stacked cards. Measured on the real board: column cards sit ~44px apart and the circle is r=40, so the pools MUST overlap. This shows the current truth; it is not a bug report. Row separation does not address it — a column spans depths.

scenarios.name: THE CASCADE — rows then a column
scenarios.proves: The complete act's SHAPE: four sections in order, the show pulsing once per section (GAP-006) and the light set replacing without being freed. THIS IS WHERE CHART E'S MISSING TRAVEL IS VISIBLE — watch whether the light moves between sections or cuts.

scenarios.name: THE CASCADE, with row separation
scenarios.proves: The same cascade with the S16 reveal simulated — each section's row opens as it takes the light, and closes as the next one does. This is the whole act as the design intends it to look.

scenarios.name: Six lights against four initial origins
scenarios.proves: The subdivision allocator — k0 is 4, so six lights force it to split

scenarios.name: A deep board, the bottom row lit
scenarios.proves: Long beams, and Q117 — a beam never points upward

scenarios.name: MOCKED SOLO TRIGGER — one card becomes active
scenarios.proves: Chart T's momentary cue at Q245=(c)'s SHALLOWER dim. The spotlight fires whenever a card becomes active in ordinary play, including every placement — Q245's own scrutiny note is that a full-depth dim there 'means the screen pulses dark on every single card you place'. Compare the dim depth against S1.

scenarios.name: ONE light on a card face — GATE G2.2
scenarios.proves: THE READABILITY CONSTRAINT (design 14b.3). Hold this and read the rank, the suit pip and the art square THROUGH the circle. ⚠ THE GLOW IS NOT IN THIS TOOL YET and QR9=(c) makes the glow the thing that draws the disc's light, where circle_inner_alpha lives — so this shows the light layer's contribution with nothing over it, and G2.2 cannot be finally settled here until the glow is in.

scenarios.name: The accessibility floor — set fx_intensity to 0
scenarios.proves: GATE G2.4: Q83 says fx_intensity=0 'keeps beams glow and dim'. Take the fx_intensity knob to 0 and THE DIM MUST STILL STAND.

scenarios.name: THE PER-SECTION PULSE at normal pacing — turn 'play' on
scenarios.proves: GAP-006, and it is the first thing to judge. In a real act this beat is 1-3 frames because get_delay() is already compressed; here it runs at base_delay uncompressed. If it reads as a flash rather than a spotlight, the knobs are spotlight_hold_fraction and the two dim fractions — and spotlight_dim_target = 0 is the off switch, which keeps every beam, circle and glow.
